question.text: Research by Rosenberg, Reid and Lanstein (1985) and subsequent studies established the 'Value Anomaly'. Which relationship is at the heart of this anomaly?

answer.text: High P/E ratio stocks have systematically outperformed low P/E stocks.
Stocks with low dividend yield outperform those with high dividend yield over long horizons.
A POSITIVE relationship between book-value-to-price (BV/P) ratio and future returns - stocks with high BV/P have generated superior risk-adjusted returns.
Growth stocks consistently beat value stocks across all developed markets.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 3.4.3, the Value Anomaly refers to a positive relationship between book-value-to-price ratio and future stock returns: high BV/P (i.e., 'value') stocks generated superior risk-adjusted returns. This contradicts semi-strong EMH and underpins value investing (Benjamin Graham, Warren Buffett). The Trap: Options A and D reverse value/growth. Option B misstates the dividend relationship. Only C captures the documented BV/P effect. Cross-Exam Context: Fama-French HML factor covers this in XXI-B and XV. XIX-C: distressed/special-situations Cat I/II AIFs explicitly harvest deep-value mispricing in situations of coverage abandonment or complex capital structures. Manager's Pro-Tip: When designing a value-focused Cat III strategy, pair book-to-price screens with quality filters (ROCE, accruals) - raw BV/P in Indian mid/small caps often flags value traps rather than true anomalies.
